hypothesis.statement: The SS record's causal framing of this residual is WRONG and that is what the next lane needs. It says 'the target spends 4 more bytes on saves and 4 fewer on locals', which invites a local-area attack. Measured this run: the byte-swap scratch block sits at 32..43 in BOTH streams (slot rows 32-43 pair one-for-one at equal use counts) and the frame is 72 in BOTH, so the LOCAL AREAS ARE IDENTICAL and there is no 4-byte local difference to compensate. The target's sixth callee-saved register is paid for out of the frame's existing 8-align SLACK, not out of the locals: 6 saves put its stmw base at 72-24=48, 5 saves put ours at 72-20=52, and the same frame absorbs both. So the whole residual is a single allocator DEMAND question - does MWCC keep the loop-invariant -1 in a callee-saved register across loop 2 - and every frame-shaped lever is addressing a difference that does not exist.
